subQuestions.questionText: Which formula shows the way in which atoms are bonded in a molecule but does not show all the bond lines?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
A condensed structural formula shows how atoms are bonded but omits some of the bond lines.

subQuestions.questionText: Which ONE of the following compounds has hydrogen bonds between its molecules?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Only the alcohol (with an –OH group bonded to H) can form hydrogen bonds between its molecules.

subQuestions.questionText: Consider the compound below. It is a branched-chain carbonyl compound: a chain of carbon atoms with a ketone (C=O) group and a methyl (CH₃) branch. Which ONE of the following is the IUPAC name of this compound? *(Refer to the condensed structure in the original question paper.)*
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
The compound is 2-methylpentan-3-one: a five-carbon ketone chain with the carbonyl on C3 and a methyl branch on C2.

subQuestions.questionText:
A 2 g piece of magnesium reacts with EXCESS hydrochloric acid according to the following balanced equation:
Mg(s) + 2HCℓ(aq) → MgCℓ₂(aq) + H₂(g)
Which ONE of the following changes will INCREASE the YIELD of H₂(g)?

options.B: Use a 3 g piece of magnesium.
options.C: Use a greater volume of the acid.
options.D: Use a higher concentration of the acid.

subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
The acid is in excess, so more magnesium (the limiting reactant) produces a greater yield of H₂. Crushing or changing the acid only affects rate, not yield.

subQuestions.questionText: The Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution curve P represents the number of molecules against kinetic energy for a certain reaction. Curve Q is obtained after a change was made to one reaction condition. Curve Q has the same shape and the same position of the activation energy (Eₐ) as curve P, but a higher peak that shows a greater total number of molecules. Which ONE of the following changes resulted in curve Q? *(Refer to the distribution graph in the original question paper.)*

options.D: Increase in the concentration of the reactants

subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
An increase in reactant concentration increases the total number of molecules without shifting the energy distribution or the activation energy.

subQuestions.questionText:
The expression for the equilibrium constant (Kc) of a hypothetical reaction is given as follows:
Kc = [X]³ / ([Y]²[Z])
Which ONE of the following equations for a reaction at equilibrium matches the above expression?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Z and Y are reactants (in the denominator) and X is an aqueous product (in the numerator, power 3). The solid Q(s) is omitted from the Kc expression.

subQuestions.questionText:
Two dilute acids of equal concentrations are added to separate test tubes: 100 cm³ HCℓ(aq) and 100 cm³ CH₃COOH(aq). Consider the following statements regarding these acids:
I: The pH of each is less than 7.
II: Both will react at the same rate with 5 g of magnesium powder.
III: Both will neutralise the same number of moles of NaOH(aq).
Which of the statements above is/are TRUE?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Both are acids (pH < 7) and, at equal concentration and volume, contain the same number of moles of acid to neutralise NaOH. Statement II is false: the strong acid HCℓ reacts faster than the weak acid CH₃COOH.

subQuestions.questionText: Which ONE of the following is the conjugate base of H₂PO₄⁻?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
The conjugate base is formed by removing one H⁺ from H₂PO₄⁻, giving HPO₄²⁻.

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram represents a voltaic cell with a Zn(s) electrode in ZnSO₄(aq) and a Cu(s) electrode in CuSO₄(aq), connected by a voltmeter (V) and a KCℓ(aq) salt bridge. The salt bridge junctions between the two half-cells are labelled X (on the zinc side) and Y (on the copper side). Which ONE of the following correctly describes the movement of ions in the cell? *(Refer to the cell diagram in the original question paper.)*
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
Negative ions (Cℓ⁻) from the salt bridge move towards the anode (zinc, X side), i.e. from Y to X, to maintain electrical neutrality.

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram represents a cell that is used for the refining of copper. An electrode X and an electrode of impure copper are connected to a power supply and dip into a CuSO₄(aq) solution. Which ONE of the following statements is TRUE? *(Refer to the electrolytic cell diagram in the original question paper.)*

options.C: X is the electrode where oxidation takes place.
options.D: X is connected to the positive terminal of the power supply.

subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
X is the cathode (pure copper), where Cu²⁺ ions are reduced and deposited, so its mass increases.

The melting points and boiling points of four straight-chain ALKANES are shown in the table below.

subQuestions.questionText: Write down the general conclusion that can be made about the melting points of straight-chain alkanes.

As the chain length/number of C atoms/molecular mass/surface area/strength of the intermolecular forces increases, the melting points increase. ✓✓

subQuestions.questionText:
The reaction of 15 g of an IMPURE sample of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃, with EXCESS hydrochloric acid, HCℓ, of concentration 1,0 mol·dm⁻³, is used to investigate the rate of a reaction. The balanced equation is:
CaCO₃(s) + 2HCℓ(aq) → CaCℓ₂(aq) + H₂O(ℓ) + CO₂(g)
The volume of CO₂(g) produced is measured at regular intervals. A sketch graph of total volume of CO₂ produced versus time rises with a decreasing gradient and levels off at a maximum volume X after time t₃ (with reference times t₁, t₂ and t₃ marked on the time axis). *(Refer to the volume-versus-time graph in the original question paper.)*
Define the term reaction rate.
subQuestions.memoText:
ANY ONE (2 or 0):
• Change in concentration of products/reactants per (unit) time. ✓✓
• Change in amount/number of moles/volume/mass of products or reactants per (unit) time.
• Amount/number of moles/volume/mass of products formed/reactants used per (unit) time.
• Rate of change in concentration/amount of moles/number of moles/volume/mass.
NOTE: Give the mark for per unit time only if in context of reaction rate.

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason why the gradient of the graph decreases between t₂ and t₃.
subQuestions.memoText: Reaction rate decreases./Concentration of HCℓ decreases./Concentration of reactant decreases./Reactants are used up./Mass of CaCO₃ decreases or is used up. ✓

subQuestions.questionText: Changes in the graph between t₁ and t₂ are due to temperature changes within the reaction mixture. Is the reaction EXOTHERMIC or ENDOTHERMIC?

subQuestions.questionText: The percentage purity of the sample is 82,5%. Calculate the value of X on the graph assuming that the gas is collected at 25 °C. Take the molar gas volume at 25 °C as 24 000 cm³.

Mark 1: m(pure CaCO₃) = (82,5/100) × 15 = 12,375 g ✓
Mark 2: Divide by 100 g·mol⁻¹ → n(pure CaCO₃) = 12,375/100 = 0,124 mol ✓
Mark 3: Use mol ratio n(CO₂) = n(CaCO₃) = 0,124 mol ✓
Mark 4: Multiply n(CO₂) by 24 000 cm³ → V(CO₂) = 0,124 × 24 000 ✓
Mark 5 (final answer): X = 2 976 cm³ (≈ 2,98 dm³) ✓
Range: 2 880 to 2 970 cm³ / 2,88 to 2,97 dm³.

subQuestions.questionText:
Consider the balanced equation below for a hypothetical reaction that takes place in a sealed 2 dm³ container at 300 K:
2P(g) + Q₂(g) ⇌ 2PQ(g)
Define the term chemical equilibrium.
subQuestions.memoText:
(The stage in a chemical reaction when the) rate of forward reaction equals the rate of reverse reaction. (2 or 0) ✓✓
OR: (The stage in a chemical reaction when the) concentrations of reactants and products remain constant. (2 or 0)

subQuestions.questionText: The amount of each substance present in the equilibrium mixture at 300 K is: P = 0,8 mol; Q₂ = 0,8 mol; PQ = 3,2 mol. The temperature of the container is now increased to 350 K. When a NEW equilibrium is established, it is found that 1,2 mol P(g) is present in the container. Is the heat of the reaction (ΔH) POSITIVE or NEGATIVE?
subQuestions.memoText: Negative ✓

subQuestions.questionText: Use Le Chatelier's principle to explain the answer to QUESTION 6.2.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
• Increase in temperature favours an endothermic reaction. (Accept: Decrease in temperature favours an exothermic reaction.) ✓
• Reverse reaction is favoured./Concentration of reactants increases./Concentration of products decreases. ✓
• (Forward) reaction is exothermic. (Accept: Reverse reaction is endothermic.) ✓

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the equilibrium constant at 350 K.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark scheme (8 marks) — using number of moles (OPTION 1):
a) Initial n(P) = 0,8; n(Q₂) = 0,8; n(PQ) = 3,2 (from table). ✓
b) Change in n(P) = equilibrium n(P) − initial n(P) = 1,2 − 0,8 = 0,4 mol. ✓
c) Using ratio P : Q₂ : PQ = 2 : 1 : 2 → change n(Q₂) = 0,2; change n(PQ) = 0,4. ✓
d) Equilibrium n(Q₂) = 0,8 + 0,2 = 1,0 mol; Equilibrium n(PQ) = 3,2 − 0,4 = 2,8 mol. ✓
e) Divide equilibrium amounts by 2 dm³: [P] = 1,2/2 = 0,6; [Q₂] = 1,0/2 = 0,5; [PQ] = 2,8/2 = 1,4 mol·dm⁻³. ✓
f) Kc = [PQ]² / ([Q₂][P]²) ✓
g) Kc = (1,4)² / [(0,5)(0,6)²] ✓
h) Kc = 10,89 (10,889) ✓
No Kc expression, correct substitution: Max. Wrong Kc expression: Max.

subQuestions.questionText: How will the equilibrium constant calculated in QUESTION 6.2.3 be affected when the volume of the container is decreased at constant temperature? Choose from INCREASES, DECREASES or REMAINS THE SAME. Give a reason for the answer.

Sulphuric acid, H₂SO₄, ionises in two steps as follows:
I: H₂SO₄(aq) + H₂O(ℓ) ⇌ HSO₄⁻(aq) + H₃O⁺(aq)   Ka = 1 × 10³
II: HSO₄⁻(aq) + H₂O(ℓ) ⇌ SO₄²⁻(aq) + H₃O⁺(aq)   Ka = 1 × 10⁻²
Define an acid in terms of the Lowry-Brønsted theory.
subQuestions.memoText: (It is a) proton/H₃O⁺ (ion)/H⁺ (ion) donor. ✓✓

subQuestions.questionText: The conductivity of solutions of HSO₄⁻(aq) and H₂SO₄(aq) are compared. Which solution will have a LOWER conductivity? Explain the answer.

subQuestions.questionText: The pH of a hydrochloric acid solution, HCℓ(aq), is 1,02 at 25 °C. Calculate the concentration of the HCℓ(aq).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark scheme (3 marks):
pH = −log[H₃O⁺] ✓
[H₃O⁺] = 10⁻pH = 10⁻¹·⁰² = 0,0955 mol·dm⁻³ ✓
Therefore [HCℓ] = 0,0955 mol·dm⁻³ (≈ 0,096/0,1 mol·dm⁻³) ✓

subQuestions.questionText:
This HCℓ solution reacts with sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃, according to:
2HCℓ(aq) + Na₂CO₃(aq) → 2NaCℓ(aq) + CO₂(g) + H₂O(ℓ)
50 cm³ of the HCℓ solution is added to 25 cm³ of a 0,075 mol·dm⁻³ Na₂CO₃ solution. Calculate the concentration of the EXCESS HCℓ in the new solution.
subQuestions.memoText:
POSITIVE MARKING FROM 7.2.1. Mark scheme (8 marks):
Mark 1: Formula c = n/V (or cₐVₐ/c_bV_b = nₐ/n_b). ✓
Mark 2: n(Na₂CO₃) = 0,075 × 0,025 = 0,001875 mol. ✓
Mark 3: n(HCℓ)initial = 0,0955 × 0,05 / 0,096 × 0,05 = 0,00475 mol. ✓
Mark 4: Use ratio n(HCℓ)used = 2n(Na₂CO₃) = 2(0,001875) = 0,0038 mol. ✓
Mark 5: n(HCℓ)excess = n(HCℓ)initial − n(HCℓ)used = 0,00475 − 0,0038 = 0,00095 mol. ✓
Mark 6: Substitute total volume 0,075 dm³ (50 cm³ + 25 cm³) in c = n/V. ✓
Mark 7 & 8 (final answer): c(HCℓ) = 0,00095/0,075 = 0,013 mol·dm⁻³ (1,3 × 10⁻² mol·dm⁻³). ✓✓
Range: 0,01 to 0,02 mol·dm⁻³.

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the initial emf of this cell.

The diagram shows a simplified electrolytic cell used to electroplate a ring. A ring and an electrode of pure chromium metal are connected to a power source and dip into concentrated Cr³⁺(aq) solution. *(Refer to the electrolytic cell diagram in the original question paper.)*

subQuestions.questionText: Is the pure chromium metal the ANODE or the CATHODE of the cell? Give a reason for the answer.

Anode ✓

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the total charge transferred when the mass of the pure chromium changes by 2 g.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark scheme (5 marks):
Mark 1: Substitute M = 52 g·mol⁻¹ in n = m/M → n(Cr) = 2/52 = 0,038 mol. ✓
Mark 2: Use mol ratio n(electrons) : n(Cr) = 3 : 1 → n(e⁻) = 3(0,038) = 0,115 mol. ✓
Mark 3: Number of electrons = n × 6,02 × 10²³ = 0,115 × 6,02 × 10²³ = 6,946 × 10²². ✓
Mark 4: Total charge Q = number of electrons × 1,6 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 6,95 × 10²² × 1,6 × 10⁻¹⁹. ✓
Mark 5 (final answer): Q = 11 113,85 C. ✓
Range: 11 076,8 to 11 580 C.
